title.value: PyNM: a Lightweight Python implementation of Normative Modeling
title.justification: The paper primarily discusses the implementation and features of PyNM, a Python package for Normative Modeling, as highlighted in its title.
title.quote: Harvey, & Dumas. (2022). PyNM: a Lightweight Python implementation of Normative Modeling. Journal of Open Source Software , 7 (80), 4321. 1

extractions.description: PyNM is a lightweight Python package designed to simplify the implementation of Normative Modeling. It provides a user-friendly interface, automatic dataset handling, and offers various model options for neuroimaging and psychiatry studies to better understand individual deviations from normative data.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on a neuroimaging tool rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development.

applications.justification: The paper describes the use of the PyNM package to improve neuroimaging analysis, specifically in the context of normative modeling to identify individual deviations from normative data.
applications.quote: The basic idea underpinning Normative Modeling is to fit a model on the controls (or a subset of them) of a dataset, and then apply it to the rest of the participants.

applications.justification: The paper suggests that the PyNM tool is suitable for psychiatry studies, allowing for improved identification of individual variations from normative data within these studies.
applications.quote: Normative models map the mean and variance of a trait for a given population against a set of explanatory variables...
